texts.facts: The petitioner has filed the claim petition U/Sec. 166 of M.V. Act, 1989, against the respondents for seeking compensation on account of the grievous injuries sustained by him in the Motor Vehicle Accident. 02. The brief facts of the case of the petitioner is as under: That on 20.12.2023 at about 09.00 p.m, when the petitioner was proceeding as rider in a Scooter (SCCH-3) 3 M.V.C.No.2120/2024 bearing No.KA-09-HT-4459 along with his friend Jayashree, on Jayanagar 4th Block, 30th Cross, Bengaluru and when he reached near Cool Joint Signal, at that time all of a sudden a Goods Carrier Lorry bearing No.KA-51-B-5833 driven by its rider at a very high speed, in rash and negligent manner, came on wrong lane and dashed against the petitioner's Scooter. Due to impact, the petitioner fell down on the road and sustained grievous injuries and immediately after the accident, he was shifted to Orthopedic Center hospital, Bengaluru, wherein after first aid he was shifted to KVC hospital, Mysuru, wherein he was admitted as an inpatient and so far he has spent Rs.2,50,000/- towards medical, conveyance and nourishment expenses. Prior to the accident, the petitioner was hale and healthy and was aged about 25 years and was working as Delivery Boy and earning Rs.30,000/- p.m. Due to accidental injuries, he is not able to work and not moved around properly and unable to lead a normal life as earlier and not able to do his job and suffered huge loss of income. The accident is occurred due to rash and negligent driving of driver of offending Goods Carrier Lorry and in this regard the Jayanagara Traffic Police have registered a (SCCH-3) 4 M.V.C.No.2120/2024 case against driver of the offending Goods Carrier Lorry. The respondent No.1 is the insurer and respondent No.2 is the owner of the said offending vehicle, are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation of Rs.15,00,000/- to the petitioner together with cost and interest at the rate of 12% p.a. 03. Inspite of service of notice, the respondent No.2 remained absent and hence, was placed exparte. On service of notice, the respondent No.1 has appeared before the tribunal through its counsel and has filed objections. 04. The respondent No.2 in its objections has denied the entire case of the petitioner and admits that this respondent having insured the Lorry bearing No.KA-51-B-5833 (Goods Carrying Vehicle) in terms of the Commercial Vehicle Package Policy and the same is valid as on the date of accident and the liability of this respondent is limited to the terms and conditions of the policy. It is further denied age, avocation, income of the petitioner, manner of accident, nature of the injuries sustained Rudresh H R vs Tata Aig Gen Ins Co Ltd on 4 February, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/197915831/ 2 by the petitioner, treatment taken by the petitioner and expenses incurred by the petitioner and contended that the petitioner was riding a Motor Cycle without wearing safety headgear at the (SCCH-3) 5 M.V.C.No.2120/2024 time of alleged accident and it is violation of M.V. Act and contended that the driver of Lorry was not holding valid and effective driving licence on the date of accident and the owner of the said vehicle allowed the driver to drove the same knowing fully well that he has no valid and effective driving licence and there is no valid permit and fitness certificate to the said lorry to ply in the public place as on the date of accident and the said lorry was converted into concrete mixer without any permission from concerned authority and in this regard the Charge sheet is filed U/Sec 52 and 177 of M.V. Act and as per records the alleged accident was taken place on 20.12.2023, but complaint was lodged on 29.12.2023 and it was a hit and run case and the lorry has been falsely implicated by creating false story and manipulated Charge sheet in order to claim unlawful gain from this respondent and hence, there is clear violation of terms and conditions of the policy and provisions of M.V. Act and the compensation claimed is highly excessive and hence, pray for dismiss the petition with costs against respondent No.1. (SCCH-3) 6 M.V.C.No.2120/2024 05. Based on the aforesaid pleadings, the following Issues have been framed by my learned predecessor: - ISSUES 01. In order to prove his case, the petitioner got himself examined as PW.1 and got examined Medical Record Incharge and Doctors as PW.2 and 3 and got marked 24 documents as Ex.P.1 to 24 and closed his side evidence. 07. By way of rebuttal, the respondent No.1 got examined MRO and its Legal Manager as RW.1 and 2 and got marked 4 documents as Ex.R.1 to 4 and closed its side evidence. Heard both sides. The counsel for the respondent No.1 has relied upon the citation reported in MFA No.5013/2017 (MV) in the case of United India Insurance Company Ltd., V/s Venkatesh Babu Rudresh H R vs Tata Aig Gen Ins Co Ltd on 4 February, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/197915831/ 3 and another. 09.
texts.arguments: As per the ratio laid down by the Hon'ble Apex Court in a decision reported in 2009 ACJ 1298 in between Sarla Verma and others V/s Delhi Transport Corporation and others case the multiplier applicable to the age group of 15 to 25 is '18'. 13.
